subject: Social Habits
title: Our culture and celebrations
objectives: Children will enjoy and name familiar cultural clothes, foods, songs and dances.
Children will say that families celebrate in different ways.
content: Our clothes and food, songs and dances, and festivals and special days.
teachingActivities: Celebrate the cultures of every family in the class (Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo, and others, and different faiths); invite parents to share clothes, foods, songs and stories; never rank cultures or religions; use real objects and songs; keep any food tasting allergy-safe and halal or dietary needs respected.
learnerActivities: Join in songs and dances and name a food or clothing from home.
assessment: Observe whether each child joins a song or dance and names a food or clothing from home.
expectedOutcomes: Joins in a song or dance.
Names a food or clothing from home.
crossCurricular: Understanding the World: people and communities

lessons.title: Our clothes and food
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name familiar clothes and foods from their homes.
successCriteria: Names a clothing item or a food from home
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know about family, respect and community helpers.
resources: Pictures of local foods such as rice, yam and beans
lessons.starter: Show a piece of colourful fabric and say "This is a cloth from our homes. Our families wear lovely clothes."
teacherActivities: Show fabrics and clothes and name each one.
Show pictures of foods and say "We eat many good foods."
Let children share a food from home.
Say "We are proud of our clothes and food."
learnerActivities: Children touch and repeat the names.
Child says or points to a food.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show fabrics and clothes and name each one. Children: Children touch and repeat the names.
Step 2. Teacher: Show pictures of foods and say "We eat many good foods." Children: Children name foods they know.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children share a food from home. Children: Child says or points to a food.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We are proud of our clothes and food." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Clothes and food
practical.safety: Check all objects are clean and safe and never rank one family’s culture above another. Use pictures only for foods unless parents agree to tasting.

differentiation.support: Touch a fabric and name it together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what their family wears on a special day.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do you wear on a special day?

expectedOutcomes: Names clothes and foods from home
lessons.conclusion: Say "We love our culture" and wave.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk to your child about traditional clothes and foods your family enjoys.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name familiar clothes and foods from their homes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Songs and dances
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will join in songs and dances from different homes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know about family, respect and community helpers.
lessons.starter: Beat the drum gently and say "Listen. Can you hear the beat? Let us dance."
teacherActivities: Play the drum slowly and let children clap the beat.
Teach a simple song from the community.
Invite a child to share a song from home.
learnerActivities: Child sings or hums if they wish.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play the drum slowly and let children clap the beat. Children: Children clap with the beat.
Step 2. Teacher: Teach a simple song from the community. Children: Children join with actions.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children dance with scarves. Children: Child dances to the beat.
Step 4. Teacher: Invite a child to share a song from home. Children: Child sings or hums if they wish.

practical.title: Drum and dance
practical.safety: Keep the drum volume gentle and the floor clear. Offer a quiet space to a child sensitive to noise.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to lead a song.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.homeConnection: Sing a family song and dance together.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "join in songs and dances from different homes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Festivals and special days
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will talk about special days that families celebrate.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know about family, respect and community helpers.
resources: Pictures of festivals, birthdays and weddings
lessons.starter: Show a birthday picture and say "A birthday is a special day. Families celebrate in many ways."
teacherActivities: Show pictures of different celebrations and say what people do.
Ask "What do you do on a special day?"
Say "Every family celebrates in its own way."
Make a simple decoration for the class.
learnerActivities: Children look and say party or dance.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pictures of different celebrations and say what people do. Children: Children look and say party or dance.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What do you do on a special day?" Children: Child says or points.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Every family celebrates in its own way." Children: Children listen and nod.
Step 4. Teacher: Make a simple decoration for the class. Children: Child makes a decoration.

practical.title: Special day decorations
practical.safety: Use non-toxic washable materials and avoid assuming which festivals families celebrate. Never ask a child to join a celebration their family does not observe.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what makes a day special.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Hang the decorations and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about the special days your family celebrates.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "talk about special days that families celebrate" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our cultural party
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will join a small class party with songs, dances and decorations.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know about family, respect and community helpers.
lessons.starter: Say "Today we have a party for our class. We will sing and dance together."
teacherActivities: Wear fabrics or scarves and greet friends.
Sing and dance to the drum.
Share a song or dance from a child’s home.
learnerActivities: Child shows a song or dance.
Children wave and say thank you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Wear fabrics or scarves and greet friends. Children: Children greet each other.
Step 2. Teacher: Sing and dance to the drum. Children: Children dance and sing.
Step 3. Teacher: Share a song or dance from a child’s home. Children: Child shows a song or dance.
Step 4. Teacher: Say thank you and goodbye. Children: Children wave and say thank you.

practical.title: Class party
practical.safety: Keep the volume gentle and the floor clear. Do not require any child to wear or perform anything that their family does not agree to.

differentiation.support: Dance together and stay beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to be the drum leader.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Put away the scarves and say thank you.
lessons.homeConnection: Enjoy a family song and dance at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "join a small class party with songs, dances and decorations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?

lessons.title: Week 8 culture check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child joins in cultural activities.
successCriteria: Names a food or clothing from home
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children know about family, respect and community helpers.
lessons.starter: Sing a favourite song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: clothes and food, songs and special days.
At each station watch how the child joins in.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: clothes and food, songs and special days. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child joins in. Children: Child joins with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Culture stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep the volume gentle. Use pictures and clean fabrics only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend a song.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names clothes or foods from home; joins a song; moves to a beat; talks about a special day.

questions.question: What do you like to sing?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 8
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep sharing family culture at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child joins in cultural activities" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
